:::{#thm-sum-dot-ones}
#### The ones vector sums the entries

For every $\vx \in \reals^p$,
the sum of the elements of $\vx$ (@def-sum-of-elements)
equals the dot product of the ones vector (@def-ones-vector) with $\vx$:

$$
\sumof{\vx} = \v1 \cdot \vx.
$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\v1 \cdot \vx
&= \sumip 1 \cd x_i
&& \text{(@def-dot-product, with every entry of } \v1 \text{ equal to } 1 \text{)}
\\
&= \sumip x_i
&& \text{(multiply each entry by } 1 \text{)}
\\
&= \sumof{\vx}.
&& \text{(@def-sum-of-elements)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-sum-dot-ones}
#### The ones vector applied to a vector with three entries

For $\vx = (2, -1, 5)$ and the ones vector $\v1$ of length $3$,

$$
\ba
\v1 \cdot \vx
&= 1 \cd 2 + 1 \cd (-1) + 1 \cd 5
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\\
&= 6,
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

which is $\sumof{\vx}$, as in @exm-sum-of-elements.
Dividing by the length $p = 3$ gives the [mean](#def-mean) of the entries, $6 / 3 = 2$.

:::
